title: Injective Hom double cohomology and its Ext identification
statement:
Let $A$ be a commutative ring, let $M^\bullet$ be an integer-indexed cochain complex of $A$-modules [def-weil-abstract-derived-category], let $u\in\mathbf Z$ satisfy $M^a=0$ for $a>u$, let $N$ be an $A$-module, and let $N[0]\to I^\bullet$ be any injective resolution [def-sp-injective-resolutions] with $I^i=0$ for $i<0$. Form the commuting first-quadrant double complex [def-sp-double-complex-total]
$$D^{i,b}=\operatorname{Hom}_A(M^{u-b},I^i)\quad(i,b\geq0),\qquad D^{i,b}=0\quad\text{otherwise},$$
$$d_\mathrm{I}(f)=d_I^i\circ f,\qquad d_\mathrm{II}(f)=(-1)^{b-u+1}f\circ d_M^{u-b-1}.$$
For $i,b\geq0$, restriction of a vertical cocycle to $\ker d_M^{u-b}$, followed by descent through $\operatorname{im}d_M^{u-b-1}$, induces an $A$-linear isomorphism
$$H^b_\mathrm{II}(D^{i,\bullet})\xrightarrow{\sim}\operatorname{Hom}_A(H^{u-b}(M^\bullet),I^i),$$
where $H^a(M^\bullet)=\ker d_M^a/\operatorname{im}d_M^{a-1}$ [def-weil-derived-category-cohomology-functor]. These isomorphisms commute with postcomposition by every $d_I^i$, so that for every $i,b\geq0$ there is an induced $A$-linear isomorphism
$$H^i_\mathrm{I}H^b_\mathrm{II}(D)\xrightarrow{\sim}\operatorname{Ext}^i_A(H^{u-b}(M^\bullet),N).$$
Here $\operatorname{Ext}^i_A$ is the derived-category Ext of $A$-modules [def-pc-ext]; its $A$-action is induced by postcomposition with scalar multiplication on $N$. In the last isomorphism a cocycle $H^{u-b}(M^\bullet)\to I^i$ maps to its corresponding derived morphism to $N[0][i]$, and scalar multiplication by $a\in A$ is postcomposition with $a\operatorname{id}_{I^\bullet}$. These assertions include $b=0$ and $i=0$, require no finite injective dimension of $N$, and impose no Noetherian or finite-generation hypothesis.

source.place: Tag 0G20, remark-spectral-sequences-ext-variant: injective-dual cohomology and iterated-cohomology calculation in the module-target realization of its source sequence; homology.tex lemma-ss-double-complex identifies these with the first two pages.

proof.text: The displayed differentials define the double complex of [def-sp-double-complex-total]: $d_{\mathrm I}^2=0$ by $d_I^2=0$, and $d_{\mathrm{II}}^2=0$ by $d_M^2=0$, regardless of the two signs. Both mixed composites send $f$ to $(-1)^{b-u+1}d_I^i\circ f\circ d_M^{u-b-1}$, so they commute. At a zero term outside the quadrant all required composites are zero. The missing incoming vertical term at $b=0$ agrees with $\operatorname{Hom}_A(M^{u+1},I^i)=0$, since $M^{u+1}=0$.

source.place: Tag 0130, lemma-ss-double-complex; double-complex identities with the displayed differentials

proof.text: Fix $i,b\geq0$ and write $a=u-b$, $J=I^i$, $Z^a=\ker d_M^a$, $B^a=\operatorname{im}d_M^{a-1}$ and $H^a=Z^a/B^a$ [def-weil-derived-category-cohomology-functor]. A vertical cocycle is exactly a map $f:M^a\to J$ with $f d_M^{a-1}=0$, since the sign is a unit. Thus restriction to $Z^a$ descends to a map $r(f):H^a\to J$, $[z]\mapsto f(z)$. For $b>0$ a boundary is $(-1)^{b-u}g d_M^a$ and restricts to zero; for $b=0$ there are no boundaries. Hence $r$ defines the asserted map on vertical cohomology. Restriction, quotient descent, and these formulas preserve sums and scalar multiples.

source.place: Tag 0G20, remark-spectral-sequences-ext-variant, source-page calculation expanded by cycles and boundaries

proof.text: For surjectivity let $h:H^a\to J$ be $A$-linear. The inclusion $Z^a\subset M^a$ induces an inclusion $H^a=Z^a/B^a\hookrightarrow M^a/B^a$. Since $J=I^i$ is injective, its defining extension property [def-sp-injective-resolutions] extends $h$ to $\bar f:M^a/B^a\to J$. Composing with the quotient gives a map $f:M^a\to J$ killing $B^a$, hence a vertical cocycle, and $r(f)=h$. This applies also at $b=0$.

source.place: Tag 0135, definition-injective, applied to the inclusion of quotient modules

proof.text: For injectivity suppose $r(f)=0$. Then $f$ vanishes on $Z^a$, so the formula $d_M^a(x)\mapsto f(x)$ defines an $A$-linear map $\lambda:\operatorname{im}d_M^a\to J$. For $b>0$, extend $\lambda$ along $\operatorname{im}d_M^a\hookrightarrow M^{a+1}$ to $t:M^{a+1}\to J$, using precisely the injectivity property [def-sp-injective-resolutions]. Now $g=(-1)^{b-u}t$ satisfies $d_{\mathrm{II}}g=(-1)^{b-u}g d_M^a=f$, so $f$ is a boundary. If $b=0$, then $a=u$ and $Z^u=M^u$ because $M^{u+1}=0$, so $f=0$ directly. Thus the map on cohomology is injective, and together with the preceding step is an $A$-linear isomorphism.

source.place: Tag 0135, definition-injective, applied to the image inclusion; explicit boundary and upper-endpoint calculation

proof.text: The maps $r_i$ just constructed commute with postcomposition: for any $A$-linear $v:I^i\to I^{i+1}$ and any vertical cocycle $f$, both $r_{i+1}([vf])$ and $v r_i([f])$ send $[z]\in H^a$ to $v(f(z))$. In particular take $v=d_I^i$. By the definition of iterated cohomology [def-sp-double-complex-total], the $r_i$ therefore give an isomorphism of the complexes in the first index, from $H^b_{\mathrm{II}}(D)$ to $\operatorname{Hom}_A(H^a,I^\bullet)$ with differential $h\mapsto d_Ih$. Applying the $r_i$ and their inverses to cycles and boundaries gives an $A$-linear isomorphism on $i$-th cohomology, using the quotient definition [def-weil-derived-category-cohomology-functor].

source.place: Tag 0130, lemma-ss-double-complex, iterated cohomology and its induced differential

proof.text: Apply [lem-weil-pbc-ext-via-injective-resolution] in the abelian category of $A$-modules with source $H^a$ and with the given resolution $\varepsilon:N[0]\to I^\bullet$. It identifies $H^i(\operatorname{Hom}_A(H^a,I^\bullet))$ additively with the derived-category $\operatorname{Ext}_A^i(H^a,N)$. Its stated cocycle formula sends $h:H^a\to I^i$ to $Q(\varepsilon[i])^{-1}\circ Q(h):H^a[0]\to N[0][i]$, where $h$ is the chain map to $I^\bullet[i]$. Composing with the previous isomorphism proves the requested double-cohomology identification with this exact cocycle formula. The cited result includes $i=0$, when its boundary subgroup is zero.

source.place: Tag 06XR, lemma-compute-ext-resolutions (1), specialized to objects in degree zero

proof.text: Finally let $c\in A$. Multiplication $c_I$ is a chain endomorphism of $I^\bullet$, and $c_I\varepsilon=\varepsilon c_N$ because the augmentation is $A$-linear. Inverting the augmentation in the derived category gives $Q(\varepsilon[i])^{-1}Q(c_I[i])=Q(c_N[i])Q(\varepsilon[i])^{-1}$. Thus the cocycle $ch=c_I^i h$ maps to $Q(c_N[i])$ postcomposed with the class of $h$, which is exactly the scalar action specified using [def-pc-ext]. The additive isomorphism of the preceding step is consequently $A$-linear. Every construction above used only individual injective terms and the given resolution, so there is no finite injective-dimension, Noetherian, or finite-generation assumption.
